$comment: The sections of the libraries rule. stacks: the stacks a section is for; only the sections of the chosen stacks are asked about and written. The setup skill asks one question per section; apply.mjs writes the rule from the answers. platform: what to use without a library, always in the rule. use: follows the library's name on its line. notes: rules that hold while a library is chosen. Options are in the order they are offered: the first is the recommended one, the rest by popularity. firstWhen moves an option to the front when another section chose the named option. An option's packages find it in package.json (a name ending in / matches a whole scope), or in pyproject.toml for a Python section; when says when to pick it. Keep at most three options per section: a question has room for three and No library. A section with no options is one the platform covers: its answer is none unless the user names a library. The answer is an option id, none, or any other name the user gave.

sections.title: Components
sections.platform: a plain `<button>` for toggles, a native `<select>` for a short list of options.
sections.use: for menus, popovers, windows, confirmations, radio groups, bottom panels and search suggestions. The platform covers only part of these: focus, keyboard navigation and positioning stay on you.

options.name: Base UI
options.when: New projects: one library with every component, unstyled, including search suggestions.

options.name: Radix
options.when: Longest record and widest use, but no ready suggestions field.

options.name: MUI
options.when: A ready set with its own look, for apps with no design of their own.

sections.title: Forms
sections.platform: a native `<form>`, enough for a few independent fields.
sections.use: , when a form has many fields, fields that depend on each other, fields added at runtime, or errors per field as the user types. It uses the same schema as the server.

options.name: React Hook Form
options.when: The common default, with the widest use.

options.name: TanStack Form
options.when: Strict types and async validation out of the box.

sections.title: Validation
sections.platform: field attributes help the user; they protect nothing, as the server can get any request.
sections.use: for data from outside the code: request bodies, server action arguments, query values. Do not check these by hand or cast them.
notes: Validate at the edge of a route or action; code behind it gets typed data and does not check again.
Keep the library out of client code unless a form needs it, so the browser does not download it.
Validate a third-party API's response only where a wrong answer would do real harm.

options.name: Zod
options.when: The common default, and most libraries connect to it.

options.name: Valibot
options.when: Validation runs in the browser and its download matters.

sections.title: URL state
sections.platform: `URLSearchParams` for building a one-off link or an address for a request.
sections.use: for filters and anything else that reads and changes the page's query parameters. Check that it works with the framework's caching before relying on it.
notes: Changes that wait for a button, such as Apply in a panel, stay in local state until it is pressed.

options.name: nuqs
options.when: Pages with filters: typed parameters on client and server.

sections.title: Data
sections.platform: a single request from the browser with nothing shared or saved around it is a plain `fetch`.
sections.use: for data in the browser: next pages of a list, search suggestions, data shared by many components, and every write that shows at once. In an app without server rendering, for all server data.
notes: Do not write rollback by hand; a failed write puts the old data back through the library.
Writes to one item run in order, so quick clicks cannot race.
Do not fetch in `useEffect` when a query fits.

options.name: TanStack Query
options.when: The common default: paging, writes with rollback and shared cache.

options.name: SWR
options.when: Mostly reading data; a smaller download and fewer features.

options.name: RTK Query
options.when: The project is built on Redux.

sections.title: Client state
sections.platform: the URL for what a link should keep, `useState` for one component, Context for a few components under one provider. Data from the server does not go in a hand-written store.
sections.use: , when state is shared by distant components and Context re-renders are measured as a real slowdown.

options.name: Zustand
options.when: One small store, the simplest choice.

options.name: Redux Toolkit
options.when: Large apps with strict patterns, or Redux is already there.

options.name: Jotai
options.when: Many small independent pieces of state.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.platform: an error shows in place as `role="alert"`, through one shared component.
sections.use: , when a message must outlive the place it came from. Do not add a second toast library.

options.name: Sonner
options.when: The common default, with a ready-made look.

options.name: Base UI
options.when: Components come from Base UI, so nothing new to add.

options.name: React-Toastify
options.when: More built-in options, such as progress bars.

sections.title: Dates and numbers
sections.use: , only for calculations these cannot do, such as time zone arithmetic.

options.name: date-fns
options.when: Plain functions over `Date`; only what is imported is downloaded.

options.name: Day.js
options.when: Moving from Moment: nearly the same API.

sections.title: Validation
sections.platform: TypeScript types and JSDoc check nothing at run time; data from outside the code can be anything.
sections.use: for data from outside the code: request bodies, query values, files, settings from the environment, another program's output. Do not check these by hand or cast them.
notes: Validate where the data comes in (a route, a script's input); code behind it gets typed data and does not check again.
Validate a third-party API's response only where a wrong answer would do real harm.

options.name: Zod
options.when: The common default, and most libraries connect to it.

sections.title: HTTP
sections.platform: `fetch` for every HTTP call, each with a time limit (`signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms)`).
sections.use: for every HTTP call, still with a time limit on each request.

sections.title: Retries
sections.platform: one try; a failure goes back to the caller. No hand-written retry loop around `setTimeout`.
sections.use: for a call that can pass on its own (a timeout, 429, 502, 503, 504), only inside the service's client.
notes: Never wrap a client call in a second retry: the tries multiply.

options.name: p-retry
options.when: The common default: retries a promise with backoff and jitter, and stops on errors marked as final.

sections.title: HTTP mocks in tests
sections.platform: `vi.mock` on the client's function, when the request itself does not matter.
sections.use: in every test whose code sends an HTTP request. Tests never call a live service.

options.name: MSW
options.when: Mocks `fetch` and every other client at the network level (`msw/node`).

sections.title: HTTP
sections.platform: `urllib.request` only for a one-off call in a script: no sessions, no connection reuse.
sections.use: for every HTTP call. Every request passes a `timeout` (ruff `S113` fails without it).

options.name: Requests
options.when: The common default for synchronous code, with the widest use.

options.name: HTTPX
options.when: Async code, or HTTP/2; nearly the same API as Requests.

sections.title: Retries
sections.platform: one try; a failure goes back to the caller. No hand-written retry loop with `time.sleep`.
sections.use: for a call that can pass on its own (a timeout, 429, 502, 503, 504), only inside the service's client.

options.name: Tenacity
options.when: The common default: backoff, jitter and when to stop, as a decorator.

sections.title: HTTP mocks in tests
sections.platform: `unittest.mock` on the client's function, when the request itself does not matter.
sections.use: in every test whose code sends an HTTP request. Tests never call a live service.

options.name: Responses
options.when: Mocks Requests.

options.name: RESPX
options.when: Mocks HTTPX.

sections.title: Command line
sections.platform: `argparse` for a script with a few arguments. Never read `sys.argv` by hand.
sections.use: for a tool with subcommands or many options: the arguments and the help come from the function's type hints.

options.name: Typer
options.when: Typed arguments from type hints, built on Click.

sections.title: Data validation
sections.platform: `dataclasses` for data the code builds itself; they check nothing at run time.
sections.use: for data from outside the code: request bodies, files, settings from the environment, another program's output. Do not check these by hand or cast them.
notes: Validate where the data comes in; code behind it gets typed models and does not check again.
Validate a third-party API's response only where a wrong answer would do real harm.

options.name: Pydantic
options.when: The common default, and most libraries connect to it.
